title: Let only issued test cards reach the test host

blocks.text: Your team's certification harness builds each request of the network's script and sends it to the network's test host. Two things went wrong last month. A tester checked the link with a card from their own wallet, and the security team had to treat the build logs, the dumps and a ticket as card data. Another case, keyed by hand, came back with `14` instead of the answer it was written to test, and a session slot went with it.

The network has issued test card ranges for this certification, each given as the leading digits its cards share. Every request now passes through `TestCardGuard.check` before it is sent. Finish the three methods marked `TODO` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/TestCardGuard.java`:

items: `panOf`: the card number a request carries;
`isTestCard`: whether the harness may send it;
`refusal`: the text of the refusal, which goes to the build log.

blocks.text: When you're done, only cards the network issued for this certification reach the test host, keyed or swiped, and a refusal tells the tester which card it stopped. About fifteen lines in total.
The tests use other test ranges and card numbers than the lesson.

cases.says: a request with a card from an issued test range, keyed or not, and a message with no card at all are sent unchanged
a number from no issued range, with a wrong check digit, is refused
a number with a correct check digit is still refused when no issued range holds it, because the check digit says nothing about who owns the card
a number from an issued range with a wrong check digit is refused, so a mistyped test card never reaches the host
a swiped purchase with no field 2 is judged by the card number in its track 2, with either separator
the refusal lets the tester recognise the card without putting its full number into the build log

origin.section: 10.4. A Test Card Is Issued for Testing, and the Luhn Check Only Says It Is Well Formed

concepts: Only cards issued for testing go to a test host; the Luhn check digit only catches typing errors, and a real card number in a log puts every copy under PCI DSS.
